analysis.title: Monday Kick-off
key_insights: Last week's market narrative shifted from AI demand strength to concern over the scale and cost of financing the AI build-out. Anthropic's filing, record SK hynix results and strong Microsoft Azure growth supported semiconductors early, but muted reactions to Alphabet and Amazon refocused investors on free cash flow, leverage and capex intensity.

US equities closed lower Friday, driven by the AI trade, and the Nasdaq had its worst session since June. Pictet reads the move as internal rotation rather than wholesale derisking, since 9 of 11 S&P 500 sectors rose for the week.

Gold fell 3.3% on Friday to below USD 4,000, its worst day since June. US Treasuries were stronger. Crude rose 2.9% on the week but fell Monday morning on hopes around Iran war talks entering a third day.
US Q3 GDP came in at 3.4% and September PCE inflation at 3.6% YoY, showing resilient growth alongside sticky inflation. China NBS Manufacturing PMI slipped into contraction in October.

Intel fell sharply on weak guidance. Brazilian assets sold off after Lula's victory and its contested aftermath, and Israel's inconclusive election revived coalition uncertainty. Brent rose back above USD 115/bbl on Gulf tensions, tanker disruptions and strikes near Saudi energy infrastructure.

Central banks delivered a global hawkish pause. The Fed held at 3.75%-4.00% with two dissents in favour of a hike, and Chair Warsh gave no forward guidance and nothing pushed back against a December hike. Markets priced a 74% chance of a December Fed hike and at least two more next year.

The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5% after September's 25bp hike, with inflation at 3.8% on energy. Markets priced an 85% chance of a December hike and two more in 2027. Lagarde warned indebted countries on fiscal rules and noted tools exist for disorderly markets, which helped keep the French 10-year yield below 4.90%.

The BoJ held at 1.25% in an 8-1 vote, said underlying inflation is generally consistent with its 2% target, and raised FY2027 inflation forecasts. Further normalisation is likely but gradual given weak growth. The RBNZ surprisingly held at 2.75% in a 4-3 vote despite over 90% pricing of a hike beforehand, and December hike odds rebounded to about 75% after a sharp drop.

Pictet's Exposure Optimisation Model raised suggested global equity exposure to 71% from 66%. US rose to 73% from 67% and Europe to 69% from 58%, while Asia fell to 60% from 67%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average switched into bear mode at Friday's close.

Precious metals face pressure from persistently high real yields and a firmer US dollar, and short-term momentum has weakened. Longer-term technical structures in gold and silver have been tested but not broken, and flows show early improvement.

November has historically been a strong month for US equities, and midterm years bring more volatility before election day with a more constructive month after it. Rates, gold and oil have diverged from their usual seasonal patterns this year.
This week's calendar includes the US midterms on Tuesday Nov 3, ISM manufacturing and services, the jobs report on Friday Nov 6, RBA and BoE decisions, and Apple and AMD earnings.

tension_points.bull_case: AI demand remains exceptionally strong, supported by Anthropic's filing, record SK hynix results and strong Azure growth at Microsoft.
tension_points.bear_case: Muted reactions to Alphabet and Amazon moved focus to free cash flow, leverage and capex intensity, and the Nasdaq had its worst session since June on Friday.

tension_points.bull_case: The Fed sees strong growth as not necessarily inflationary and financial conditions as not yet restrictive, and the ECB sees no second-round effects.
tension_points.bear_case: Two Fed dissents favoured a hike, markets price December hikes at 74% for the Fed and 85% for the ECB, and inflation stays sticky at 3.6% PCE and 3.8% in the euro area.
